introduction: A carry-patch rebuild applies patch branches onto the upstream base inside a detached, per-run git worktree instead of the workspace's shared trunk checkout, and holds the per-workspace lock only for the steps that conflict with other operations. The rebuild algorithm and public API keep their current meaning, apart from the additive field patch_results[].source_sha and the new audit event hub.rebuild.followup.

glossary.Exception A: The case where the trunk's HEAD is the integration branch at the final ref update, so the trunk needs a hard reset to match the new tip.
glossary.Exception B: The one-time removal of a legacy _rebuild_temp branch left by a pre-upgrade run, including moving the trunk's HEAD off it.
glossary.follow-up rebuild: A rebuild job enqueued by a finished run, with submitted_by system:stale-snapshot, because a patch tip or the upstream base moved during the run.
glossary.phase one / phase two: The two lock-holding sections of a rebuild. Phase one covers the upstream fetch, base resolution, legacy migration, stale cleanup and rerere config. Phase two covers the integration-ref update, patch bookkeeping and optional push to origin.
glossary.rebuild worktree: A detached linked git worktree created for one rebuild run at <workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/<job id>. It shares the trunk's objects, refs, configuration and rr-cache but has its own HEAD, index and files.
glossary.rebuild-active guard: A per-workspace in-memory flag in internal/wslock, set by BeginRebuild and read by RebuildActive, independent of the wslock mutex. Archive and reclone refuse to run while it is set.
glossary.rerere: git's reuse-recorded-resolution feature; its cache rr-cache lives in the common git directory and MERGE_RR is per worktree.
glossary.snapshot SHA: The commit SHA that a patch branch resolved to at refs/heads/<branch> when patch application began; it is the only reference to the branch used for the rest of the run.
glossary.trunk: The non-bare clone of a workspace at <workspace_root>/<slug>/trunk, shared by the git smart HTTP server, sync, merge jobs, rollback, rerere forget and rebuilds.
glossary.wslock: The in-process per-workspace lock in internal/wslock, taken blockingly with Lock by jobs and non-blockingly with TryLock by HTTP handlers.

requirements.title: Worktree lifecycle
requirements.rationale: A per-run detached worktree lets patch application proceed without borrowing the trunk checkout and makes crash recovery a matter of deleting a directory.

criteria.condition: a rebuild reaches patch application
criteria.action: create a detached worktree with the typed WorktreeAdd call, which runs `git worktree add --detach <path> <upstream base sha>` in the trunk, where <path> is the absolute path (made absolute with filepath.Abs) <workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/<job id>

criteria.condition: the job context carries no job ID or the configured WorkspaceRoot is empty
criteria.action: use a random ID in place of the job ID when the job ID is absent, and derive the worktree path from the same parent directory as the trunk path when WorkspaceRoot is empty

build a second GitRunner with h.NewGitRunner(worktreePath) after the worktree directory exists, run log, rev-parse, cherry-pick, merge, rerere, `diff --diff-filter=U`, `commit --no-edit`, `reset --hard` to the pre-patch HEAD and worktree HEAD reads through it, and use the trunk runner only for fetch-adjacent reads, config, worktree add/remove/prune, the _rebuild_temp migration and the final ref update

for any exit path (success, conflict, transient error, early return, cancellation), remove the worktree with WorktreeRemove (`git worktree remove --force <path>`) followed by WorktreePrune (`git worktree prune`), so that `git worktree list` in the trunk shows only the trunk and the worktree directory no longer exists

criteria.condition: `git worktree remove` fails
criteria.action: fall back to os.RemoveAll(path) followed by `git worktree prune`, log the failure at warning level, and leave the job outcome unchanged
criteria.contract: The job result and status are identical to those of a run whose removal succeeded; a warning log entry naming the slug and path is written; the worktree directory is gone after the fallback

criteria.action: run worktree removal and every other cleanup step with a context derived from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) and a timeout of at most two minutes, so cleanup still executes after the job context is cancelled

provide WorktreeAdd, WorktreeRemove and WorktreePrune on gitcmd.GitRunner, the carrypatch.GitRunner interface, GitRunnerAdapter and mockGitRunner as the only place worktree commands are spelled, and change MergeNoFF to MergeNoFF(ctx, ref, message string) error where an empty message keeps git's default merge message

criteria.condition: creating the worktree fails
criteria.action: stop the run before applying any patch, leave no directory under rebuild/ for this run, release the guard and emit hub.rebuild.fail
criteria.contract: HandleRebuildJob returns a non-nil error; no integration-ref update or patch bookkeeping has occurred; the trunk HEAD, index and files are unchanged

requirements.title: The trunk is not touched
requirements.rationale: The shared trunk checkout serves clones, sync and merge jobs, so a rebuild must neither move it nor leave state in it.

criteria.action: run no `checkout`, `reset`, `cherry-pick`, `merge` or `rebase` through the trunk runner during a rebuild other than those defined by Exception A and Exception B, never create the _rebuild_temp branch, and not contain the functions currentCheckout, restoreCheckout or preflightCleanup

for any rebuild that ends in success, fail-fast conflict, continue-mode conflict or cancellation, leave the trunk's `git symbolic-ref HEAD`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git status --porcelain` output and the contents of a tracked sample file identical to their values before the run, except under Exception A and Exception B

criteria.condition: patch application finishes and phase two begins
criteria.action: force-update the integration branch to the worktree's final HEAD SHA with `git update-ref refs/heads/<integration> <sha>` using the existing UpdateRef method, never using `branch -f` and never checking the integration branch out

criteria.condition: phase two holds the workspace lock
criteria.action: read the previous integration head with `rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<integration>` immediately before the ref update and record it as previous_integration_head_sha, leaving it empty when the branch does not exist

criteria.condition: the ref update has been made under the final lock
criteria.guard: the trunk's HEAD is the symbolic ref of the integration branch (Exception A)
criteria.action: run `reset --hard HEAD` in the trunk so the index and files match the new tip, and log this at info level; in every other case run no reset in the trunk

criteria.condition: phase one runs and a local refs/heads/_rebuild_temp exists (Exception B)
criteria.action: delete that branch and log at info level that it was removed
criteria.contract: After the run `git show-ref refs/heads/_rebuild_temp` finds nothing and a log entry with the slug records the removal

criteria.condition: the _rebuild_temp migration runs and the trunk's HEAD is on _rebuild_temp
criteria.guard: any cherry-pick, merge or rebase may be in progress
criteria.action: abort any in-progress cherry-pick, merge or rebase on a best-effort basis, then move HEAD with `checkout --force <branch>` where <branch> is workspaceBranch if it exists as a local branch, else the short name of refs/remotes/origin/HEAD if that exists locally, else run `checkout --detach --force` and log a warning, before deleting _rebuild_temp

criteria.condition: the `update-ref` of the integration branch fails
criteria.action: stop phase two before any soft-deletion, compaction or push, release the lock, and emit hub.rebuild.fail
criteria.contract: HandleRebuildJob returns a non-nil error; no patch rows are changed by this run; the lock is free afterwards

requirements.title: Rerere across worktrees
requirements.rationale: Conflict resolutions recorded by the hub's rebuilds must keep replaying and stay visible to the rerere endpoints even though patches are applied in a linked worktree.

criteria.action: set rerere.enabled=true and rerere.autoupdate=true in the repository-level config with the trunk runner before creating the worktree, and not enable extensions.worktreeConfig

criteria.condition: a rebuild meets a conflict whose resolution an earlier rebuild recorded in its worktree
criteria.action: replay the recorded resolution from the shared rr-cache so the patch is applied without a reported conflict

for any resolution recorded in a rebuild worktree, list it in GET /workspaces/:slug/rerere from <trunk>/.git/rr-cache and remove it with DELETE /workspaces/:slug/rerere/*, with the entry absent from a following GET

criteria.condition: a rebuild worktree is discarded while a conflict is in progress and MERGE_RR is populated
criteria.action: leave the shared rr-cache and the endpoints' read of <trunk>/.git/MERGE_RR unaffected
criteria.contract: GET /workspaces/:slug/rerere returns 200 with the entries recorded before the discard, and <trunk>/.git/MERGE_RR holds no entry from the discarded worktree

requirements.title: Lock phases
requirements.rationale: Only the fetch and the final ref and database update write shared state, so holding the workspace lock for patch application blocks sync, rollback and merge jobs for no benefit.

criteria.condition: a rebuild job starts
criteria.action: resolve upstream credentials first, then take the blocking wslock.Lock(slug), and under that lock call BeginRebuild(slug)

criteria.condition: resolving upstream credentials fails
criteria.action: return a retryable TransientError before taking the lock or setting the guard and emit hub.rebuild.fail
criteria.contract: HandleRebuildJob returns an error of type TransientError; the lock is free and RebuildActive(slug) is false

criteria.action: perform in phase one under the lock, in this order, the upstream fetch, trunk runner creation, resolveUpstreamBase, the _rebuild_temp migration, stale worktree cleanup and rerere config, and then release the lock

criteria.condition: the rebuild is creating the worktree, listing patches, snapshotting tips or applying patches
criteria.action: hold no wslock lock, so that POST /sync, rollback, rerere forget, batch rebase and merge jobs for the same workspace acquire the lock and proceed

re-acquire wslock.Lock(slug) for phase two, perform in it the previous-head read, the integration-ref update, soft-deletion of merged_upstream patches, position compaction and the optional PushIntegration to origin, and release the lock afterwards
for any early return in phase one or phase two, release the workspace lock, and perform worktree creation, patch application and worktree removal outside any lock

criteria.condition: a rollback of the integration branch completes while patches are being applied
criteria.action: overwrite the rolled-back value with its own update-ref in phase two and record in previous_integration_head_sha the value read at phase two, with rollback and the final update serialised by the lock
criteria.contract: After the run the integration branch equals the rebuild's final HEAD SHA and previous_integration_head_sha equals the rolled-back SHA

criteria.action: after phase two, remove the worktree, run the stale-input check, emit hub.rebuild.complete, end the guard and return, in that order

requirements.title: Rebuild-active guard
requirements.rationale: Archive and reclone delete the directory the worktree lives in, and a mutex that is not held during patch application cannot stop them.

criteria.action: provide BeginRebuild(slug string) (end func(), ok bool) and RebuildActive(slug string) bool as a per-workspace flag independent of the mutex, and clear the flag on process exit because it is held only in memory

criteria.condition: BeginRebuild is called for a slug whose guard is already set
criteria.action: return ok=false without changing the existing guard, and make the rebuild return a retryable error
criteria.contract: BeginRebuild returns (nil-safe end, false); the existing guard stays set; HandleRebuildJob returns a retryable error and the job is retried by the queue

criteria.action: make the end function returned by BeginRebuild idempotent, so a second call leaves a guard set later by another run untouched
hold the guard from before stale worktree cleanup until after worktree removal on every exit path, calling end through defer

criteria.condition: an archive request reaches the clone_status == "ready" branch, TryLock succeeds and RebuildActive(slug) is true
criteria.action: release the lock and refuse the request with the existing workspace_busy message
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy; the workspace is not archived and the lock is free

criteria.condition: a reclone request obtains TryLock and RebuildActive(slug) is true
criteria.action: release the lock and refuse the request with the existing workspace_busy message
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy; the clone directory is untouched and the lock is free

criteria.condition: no rebuild is active for the workspace and the guard has been ended
criteria.action: behave exactly as before this change, so archive and reclone succeed under the same conditions as without the guard

criteria.condition: the guard is set and the lock is free
criteria.action: not consult the guard and accept their requests

requirements.title: Snapshotting patch tips
requirements.rationale: With the lock released during application, branch names can move, so applying fixed SHAs makes the run deterministic and tells the operator exactly what was applied.

criteria.condition: the patch list is sorted and before the first patch is applied
criteria.action: resolve every patch whose status is not merged_upstream, disabled or deleted with `rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}` in the trunk runner and use only the resulting SHA for `git log`, cherry-pick and merge from then on

criteria.condition: a patch uses the rebase strategy
criteria.action: list its commits with `git log --reverse --no-merges --right-only --cherry-pick <base>...<snapshot sha>` in the worktree

criteria.condition: a patch uses the merge strategy
criteria.action: call MergeNoFF(ctx, <snapshot sha>, "Merge branch '<branch name>'") in the worktree
criteria.contract: The resulting merge commit message contains the branch name

criteria.condition: a patch branch's rev-parse fails or returns empty output, or the rebase strategy yields an empty commit list
criteria.action: record the patch as skipped with reason branch_not_found and continue with the remaining patches
criteria.contract: patch_results contains an entry with status skipped and reason branch_not_found for that patch; the run does not fail because of it

criteria.condition: a tag or remote-tracking ref has the patch's name but no refs/heads/<branch> exists
criteria.action: treat the branch as not found
criteria.contract: The patch is recorded as skipped with reason branch_not_found

criteria.action: add PatchResult.SourceSHA with JSON name source_sha, omitted when empty, set for every snapshotted patch including those that then conflicted, and carry it in the job result, in the running job's progress and in the patch_results of rebuild API responses
for any patch branch that moves after its snapshot, apply exactly the commits reachable from the snapshot SHA and report that SHA as source_sha

requirements.title: Stale-input follow-up
requirements.rationale: Releasing the lock during application lets a push or a sync land mid-run, and without a rebuild-side check the change would never be rebuilt because sync only enqueues when upstream_head_sha changes.

criteria.condition: a run ends in success or in a fail-fast conflict, after worktree removal and after the phase-two lock is released
criteria.action: re-resolve refs/heads/<branch> for each patch with a snapshot SHA and status success or conflict, mark a patch stale if the result differs from its snapshot SHA, ignore patches skipped for merged_upstream, disabled or deleted, and re-run resolveUpstreamBase and mark upstream stale if it differs from the SHA the run used

criteria.condition: a run ends with a retryable error, cancellation or any failure other than a fail-fast conflict
criteria.action: skip the stale-input check and enqueue no follow-up
criteria.contract: No job with submitted_by system:stale-snapshot exists after the run and no hub.rebuild.followup event is emitted

criteria.condition: at least one patch is stale
criteria.guard: the workspace variable AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH is not "false"
criteria.action: enqueue one follow-up rebuild, and enqueue none when AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH is "false"

criteria.condition: the upstream base is stale
criteria.guard: the workspace variable AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is not "false"
criteria.action: enqueue one follow-up rebuild, and enqueue none when AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is "false"

enqueue at most one follow-up per run, carrying the same strategy, fail mode and integration branch as the original, SubmittedBy "system:stale-snapshot", a fresh nonce, Type "rebuild", Key <slug> and the running job's GroupKey read with Queue.GetByID(jobID), falling back to FormatGroupKey(slug, payload.IntegrationBranch)
criteria.contract: The new job is stored with status queued and does not start before the current job is finalised

criteria.action: add EnqueueParams.ExcludeJobID so that, when set, both the pre-insert active (type, key) duplicate query and the race-recovery query ignore the job with that ID, and leave the dedup behaviour unchanged when it is empty

criteria.condition: a follow-up rebuild is enqueued
criteria.action: emit the audit event hub.rebuild.followup, registered as a new event type for audit queries, with metadata stale_patches (branch names), upstream_stale (bool) and follow_up_job_id

criteria.condition: the Queue is nil or the follow-up enqueue returns an error
criteria.action: log a warning and leave the job outcome unchanged
criteria.contract: HandleRebuildJob returns the same result and error as without the stale check, and a warning log entry is written

requirements.title: Cancellation and crash recovery
requirements.rationale: Cleanup that reuses a cancelled context silently does nothing, and a crash must not leave state in the trunk or block later rebuilds.

criteria.condition: the job context is cancelled during patch application or a git call returns a context error
criteria.action: discard the worktree with the non-cancelled cleanup context (the forced removal also discards any in-progress cherry-pick or merge), end the guard and return a retryable TransientError
criteria.contract: HandleRebuildJob returns a TransientError; the worktree directory and registration are gone; RebuildActive(slug) is false; trunk HEAD, index and files are unchanged

criteria.condition: a rebuild runs phase one under the guard and before creating its worktree
criteria.action: remove every directory under <workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/ with os.RemoveAll and run `git worktree prune` in the trunk, replacing preflightCleanup, and log each removal at info level

criteria.condition: the hub starts, before mergeQueue.Start() in cmd/af-hub/main.go
criteria.action: call carrypatch.CleanupStaleRebuildWorktrees(ctx, workspaceRoot, logger), which removes every <workspace_root>/*/rebuild directory, runs `git worktree prune` in the matching trunk and logs each removal at info level

criteria.condition: a workspace has a rebuild directory but its trunk directory is missing
criteria.action: skip the prune for that workspace, log a warning and continue with the remaining workspaces
criteria.contract: The function returns without panicking; other workspaces are still cleaned; the rebuild directory of the trunkless workspace is removed

criteria.condition: removing a directory or pruning fails during startup cleanup
criteria.action: log the error and continue, never returning a failure that stops hub startup
criteria.contract: Hub startup proceeds to mergeQueue.Start(); an error-level or warning-level log entry names the slug and path

criteria.condition: a previous run crashed leaving a registered-but-orphaned worktree directory and a plain stale directory under rebuild/
criteria.action: remove both directories and their worktree registrations before creating the new worktree, so the next rebuild succeeds
criteria.contract: After the run `git worktree list` in the trunk shows only the trunk and the rebuild/ directory contains no stale entries

requirements.title: Coexistence with go-git, pushes and gc
requirements.rationale: The hub uses go-git on the trunk while a linked worktree is registered, and the design is only valid if those paths keep working.

criteria.condition: a git push through the hub completes while patches are being applied
criteria.action: update refs and run the go-git hard reset of the trunk working tree through updateHeadSHA, whose TryLock succeeds, leaving the rebuild worktree's HEAD, index and files unchanged

criteria.condition: POST /sync completes while patches are being applied
criteria.action: fetch upstream and update upstream_head_sha while the running rebuild keeps the base SHA it resolved in phase one
criteria.contract: The sync responds with its normal success status instead of 409 workspace_busy

criteria.action: for any registered linked rebuild worktree under the trunk, succeed in git.PlainOpen with Worktree().Reset(&git.ResetOptions{Mode: git.HardReset}), defaultSyncUpdateLocalRefFn, upstream.Fetch and DefaultPushIntegrationFunc to a local bare remote, and leave the worktree usable afterwards
never run `gc --prune=now` or `reflog expire`
for any `git gc` run while the worktree is registered, keep every object reachable only from the worktree's HEAD

criteria.condition: a rebuild has not yet completed its phase-two ref update
criteria.action: serve clones and fetches of the integration branch at its pre-rebuild tip

requirements.title: Observability, documentation and decision record
requirements.rationale: Operators need logs to follow worktree handling, and the docs and API contract must describe the narrowed workspace_busy behaviour and the new field.

criteria.action: log worktree creation and removal, per-run and startup stale worktree cleanup, and the _rebuild_temp migration at info level, each entry carrying the workspace slug and path, and log removal failures at warning level
emit hub.rebuild.complete on success and hub.rebuild.fail on every error return, with the same event shape as before this change

keep endpoints, response shapes, job records and existing audit events unchanged apart from the additive patch_results[].source_sha field and the hub.rebuild.followup event, and narrow only the documented 409 workspace_busy behaviour

update docs/api.md (Workspace Lock section, the workspace_busy row and the 409 rows for sync, rollback, rerere forget, archive and reclone) and docs/openapi.yaml to state that sync, rollback, rerere forget and batch rebase are rejected only during a rebuild's fetch phase and final phase while archive and reclone are rejected for the whole rebuild, and to list patch_results[].source_sha

rewrite steps 3 to 6 of the Rebuild algorithm in docs/carry_patch_workflow.md for the worktree flow, state that a rebuild does not change the trunk's checkout, that clones served during a rebuild see the pre-rebuild integration branch, and that a stale patch tip or upstream triggers a follow-up rebuild, and update the lock note near line 1068
remove or mark as legacy the two _rebuild_temp statements in docs/examples/AGENTS_carry_patch.md

add docs/adr/02-run-rebuilds-with-the-git-cli.md recording the decision to use the git CLI rather than go-git, with a capability table for worktree add/remove/prune, cherry-pick, non-FF merge, rerere and gc/prune as reported by go-git v5.19.1's COMPATIBILITY.md, and the condition for revisiting it (go-git gaining linked-worktree, cherry-pick, --no-ff merge and rerere support)

execution_paths.title: A rebuild succeeds without touching the trunk

steps.action: submits a rebuild request for a workspace through the rebuild API
claims the rebuild job and starts the rebuild executor
takes wslock, sets the rebuild-active guard, fetches upstream, resolves the base, runs migration and stale cleanup, and releases the lock
creates the detached worktree at <workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/<job id>, snapshots patch tips to SHAs and applies the patches in the worktree
re-acquires wslock, runs update-ref on the integration branch, soft-deletes merged patches, compacts positions and releases the lock
removes the worktree, ends the guard and emits hub.rebuild.complete with source_sha in patch_results; the trunk's HEAD, status and files are unchanged

execution_paths.title: A push during patch application produces a follow-up rebuild

steps.action: is applying snapshotted patches in its worktree with no lock held
pushes a new commit to a registered patch branch through the hub git server
updates the ref and hard-resets the trunk working tree because TryLock succeeds
finishes applying the snapshot SHAs, updates the integration ref and removes the worktree
re-resolves the patch branch, finds it differs from the snapshot SHA and enqueues a follow-up with ExcludeJobID set to its own ID
stores the follow-up as queued with submitted_by system:stale-snapshot, and the hub emits hub.rebuild.followup

execution_paths.title: A cancelled rebuild cleans up and is retried

steps.action: cancels or shuts down the hub while a rebuild is applying patches
sees a context error from a git call and switches to the non-cancelled cleanup context
force-removes the worktree, prunes registrations and ends the guard
returns a retryable TransientError, and the trunk's HEAD, index and files are unchanged
retries the job under its existing retry policy

execution_paths.title: Archive and reclone are refused during a rebuild while sync proceeds

steps.action: holds the rebuild-active guard while applying patches with the lock released
sends POST /sync for the workspace
obtains TryLock, fetches upstream, updates upstream_head_sha and responds with success
requests archive or reclone of the same workspace
obtains TryLock, sees RebuildActive is true, releases the lock and responds 409 workspace_busy
finishes, removes the worktree, ends the guard and detects the moved upstream base, enqueueing a follow-up unless AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is false

execution_paths.title: Crash leftovers are removed at startup and before the next rebuild

steps.action: crashes mid-rebuild leaving a registered worktree directory under <workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/
restarts and calls CleanupStaleRebuildWorktrees before mergeQueue.Start(), removing each rebuild directory and pruning in the matching trunk
submits a rebuild for the workspace
under the guard removes any remaining directories under rebuild/ and prunes registrations before creating its worktree
completes the rebuild and leaves `git worktree list` showing only the trunk

execution_paths.title: A recorded rerere resolution replays in the next rebuild

steps.action: resolves a conflict recorded by a rebuild in its worktree under the shared rr-cache
submits a second rebuild of the workspace
applies the same patch in a new worktree and replays the recorded resolution with no conflict reported
calls GET /workspaces/:slug/rerere and sees the entry, then DELETE /workspaces/:slug/rerere/* and sees it forgotten

execution_paths.title: A fail-fast conflict leaves the trunk untouched and a legacy branch is migrated

steps.action: upgrades the hub while the trunk has a leftover _rebuild_temp branch checked out, then submits a fail-fast rebuild
under the phase-one lock aborts any in-progress operation, moves the trunk to the workspace branch with checkout --force and deletes _rebuild_temp
applies patches in a worktree, hits a conflict on one patch and stops with a fail-fast conflict result
removes the worktree, runs the stale-input check and emits the conflict outcome, with the integration branch unchanged and the trunk's HEAD and files unchanged after the migration
